title: Human Sexual Reproductive System
seo_title: Secondary 2 Science: Human Reproduction Worksheets (Lower Secondary Science with Answers)
standard_text: Recognise that fertilisation is the fusion of the nuclei of an egg and a sperm and that sexual reproduction passes on genetic information; state the physical changes at puberty caused by hormones; describe the parts of the male and female reproductive systems, fertilisation and the menstrual cycle; recognise the harmful effects of substance abuse, including on the foetus; outline temporary and permanent methods of birth control; state the consequences of sexually transmitted infections such as syphilis, gonorrhoea and AIDS (summary of the MOE Lower Secondary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 2 science worksheets for Singapore students on human reproduction: reproductive systems, fertilisation, puberty, the menstrual cycle, birth control and STIs. With answers.
key_big: Fertilisation: a sperm nucleus fuses with an egg nucleus.
key_sub: It usually happens in the oviduct.
body_html:
How to think about it

A new individual begins when the nucleus of a sperm fuses with the nucleus of an egg.

  • Male: testes make sperm; sperm ducts carry them; glands add fluid to make semen. Female: ovaries release eggs; fertilisation happens in the oviduct; the foetus develops in the uterus.
  • The child gets genetic information from both parents, so it is similar to but different from them.
  • Puberty changes are caused by sex hormones. In a 28-day menstrual cycle, an egg is released at about day 14.
  • Birth control can be temporary (condom, pill) or permanent (vasectomy, tubal ligation). Bacterial STIs can be cured with antibiotics; AIDS cannot.
Example

Where does fertilisation usually happen?

The egg meets sperm on its way to the uterus

Answer: in the oviduct

Example

Is a vasectomy temporary or permanent?

The sperm ducts are cut and tied

Answer: permanent

Common mistakes

  • Saying fertilisation happens in the uterus. It usually happens in the oviduct.
  • Saying the sperm duct makes sperm. The testes make sperm.
  • Thinking AIDS can be cured with antibiotics. It is caused by a virus.
  • Thinking the egg is released on day 1. Day 1 is the start of menstruation.

faq.a: Usually in the oviduct (fallopian tube). The fertilised egg then attaches to the lining of the uterus.

faq.q: What causes the changes at puberty?
faq.a: Sex hormones made by the testes in boys and the ovaries in girls.

faq.q: Can all STIs be cured with antibiotics?
faq.a: No. Syphilis and gonorrhoea, caused by bacteria, can be cured with antibiotics. AIDS, caused by a virus (HIV), cannot.
